_how_to_update: The 28th monthly task rewrites this file for the next month (matching that month's sowing calendar), adds the new photos to site/img, runs site-src/build.py and pushes. Keep wording in June's voice, British English, no hyphens.
intro: The beds are going to sleep, but there's still plenty to get in the ground before the frosts set in properly.
quote: Leave your parsnips in until after the first frost. The cold turns them sweet.

sow.name: Garlic
sow.note: Get every clove in this month. It needs the cold to split into a bulb.

sow.name: Broad beans
sow.note: A hardy variety like Aquadulce, straight into the bed, for the earliest beans next spring.

sow.name: Onion sets
sow.note: Autumn sets, just the tips showing above the soil.

sow.name: Pea shoots
sow.note: A tray on the windowsill. You'll be cutting them in about two weeks.

plant.name: Bare root fruit bushes
plant.note: Currants, gooseberries and raspberries are cheapest now, sold bare root.

plant.name: Rhubarb
plant.note: Plant a crown with the buds just at soil level, then leave it alone for a year.

jobs: Net kale and sprouts against pigeons
Bag up fallen leaves for leaf mould
Check bonfire piles for hedgehogs before lighting

recipe.title: Honey roast parsnips
steps: Cut the parsnips into long wedges and toss with the oil, salt and pepper.
Roast at 200°C (180°C fan) for 30 minutes, turning once.
Drizzle over the honey, add the thyme and roast 10 minutes more until sticky.
